(Today through Wednesday)...
Issued at 233 AM EDT Thu Sep 10 2026

Showers and embedded thunderstorms will impact the region for much 
of the day as a wave of low pressure rides along a frontal boundary 
across the southern half of central Indiana. The front will shift 
south and wash out by Friday but remnant moisture will interact with 
a weak upper low to produce additional chances for rain across the 
Ohio Valley Friday night and Saturday.

Upper ridging will flex back into the area this weekend and into 
early next week with warm temperatures. A more organized threat for 
rain and storms will accompany a cold front on Tuesday with cooler 
air following for the second half of next week.

Today through Saturday

After a largely quiet first half of the night...scattered convection 
was developing across the lower Wabash Valley early this morning 
ahead of a cluster of storms moving east of KSTL. Temperatures at 
06Z were in the upper 60s and lower 70s with patchy fog developing 
as well.

The developing convection early this morning is being aided by 
increasing warm advection and 850mb flow on the south side of a 
quasi-stationary boundary located just south of I-70. Expect a 
steady increase in coverage as an ongoing convective cluster over 
southern Illinois shifts east through the predawn hours. With PWATs 
near 2 inches currently across the southern portions of the forecast 
area and a front that will move little over the next several 
hours...storms will be efficient rainfall producers as they track 
across the southern tier of counties from Vincennes to Seymour 
through daybreak with lighter rainfall rates further north.

The first area of shower and storms will move east but once the 
front pushes further south...winds will shift to northerly. of the
forecast by late morning but will likely be followed by a second 
cluster currently across eastern Kansas and western Missouri and 
poised to track into the southern half of the forecast area this 
afternoon. The arrival of an upper wave from the northwest will 
buckle heights aloft and should allow for the frontal boundary to 
resume southward progression during the afternoon. The heaviest 
rainfall rates with the afternoon storms may just graze far 
southern counties and focus more across far southern Indiana into 
Kentucky where a more unstable airmass will reside. 
Regardless...rain chances will linger for much of the day with an 
abundance of lower clouds.

Clouds will diminish from the north tonight as weak high pressure 
and deeper subsidence expand into the area. Patchy fog may again be 
a factor for early Friday with near calm winds even as drier air 
advects into the region. The aforementioned frontal boundary will 
wash out south of the Ohio River on Friday leaving an axis of 
remnant moisture. As a developing upper low lifts into the mid 
Mississippi Valley late Friday...the moisture will be pulled back 
north into the area with scattered showers and storms impacting the 
southeast half of the forecast area in particular Friday night into 
Saturday as the upper low pivots across the region. 

Temps...clouds and rain today will keep temperatures closer to early 
September normals in the upper 70s and lower 80s with similar 
readings for Friday as well. The resumption of return southerly flow 
for Saturday will bring a warmer and subtly more humid airmass back 
into the area with mid 80s. 

Saturday Night through Wednesday

The deeper moisture plume will shift east of the region Saturday 
night as ridging aloft expands back north for late weekend. This 
will stall a weak frontal boundary to our north over the lower Great 
Lakes before lifting back north as a warm front early next week in 
response to low pressure developing over the High Plains. This will 
allow for a brief return of a hotter and more humid airmass with 
highs climbing back to near 90 degrees Monday and Tuesday across the 
southern half of the forecast area.

The aforementioned surface low will track into Ontario on Tuesday 
pulling a cold front into the region with a better chance at showers 
and storms. Model trends are now supporting the boundary becoming 
nearly stationary across the Ohio Valley through the middle of next 
week as it runs into the retreating upper level ridge to the south. 
The boundary may linger until a much stronger cold front running in 
tandem with a sharp upper level wave dives through the area late 
next week. In the wake of this frontal passage...the first 
opportunity for a cooler early Fall airmass is becoming increasingly 
likely for the region by next weekend.
